questions.question_text: An asset costs $\$52\,000$. Straight-line depreciation removes $\$6500$ per year; declining-balance depreciation is $16\%$ p.a. What is the **lower** of the two salvage values after $3$ years, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Chose the straight-line value, but the declining-balance value is lower after $3$ years.
Used $n = 2$ in $52\,000(0.84)^{n}$ instead of $n = 3$.
Used $n = 4$ in $52\,000(0.84)^{n}$ instead of $n = 3$.

questions.question_text: A $\$15\,000$ asset can be depreciated by $\$1900$ per year (straight-line) or at $14\%$ p.a. (declining balance). What is the **total depreciation** after $4$ years under the declining-balance method, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Gave the salvage value $15\,000(0.86)^{4}$ instead of the value lost.
Gave the straight-line total $1900 \times 4$ rather than the declining-balance total.
Took $14\%$ of the purchase price four times, instead of $14\%$ of the current value each year.

questions.question_text: An asset costing $\$20\,000$ is depreciated either by $\$3200$ per year (straight-line) or at $24\%$ p.a. (declining balance). After how many whole years is the straight-line value first below the declining-balance value?

options.why: Stopped at the last year in which the straight-line value is still the higher one.
Went one year past the first year in which the straight-line value is lower.
Compared the amounts of depreciation rather than the values remaining.

questions.solution_text:
At $n = 4$: straight-line $= 20\,000 - 3200(4) = \$7200$; declining balance $= 20\,000(0.76)^{4} = \$6672.44$
At $n = 5$: straight-line $= 20\,000 - 3200(5) = \$4000$; declining balance $= 20\,000(0.76)^{5} = \$5071.05$

The straight-line value is first the lower one after $5$ years.

options.why: Took $16\%$ of the purchase price; that is the declining-balance loss, not the straight-line amount.
Read the purchase price off the vertical axis instead of the yearly loss.
Halved the purchase price instead of dividing it by the $9$-year life shown.

questions.solution_text:
The straight line starts at $\$18\,000$ and reaches $\$0$ after $9$ years.
$D = \dfrac{18\,000}{9}$
$= \$2000$ per year

questions.question_text: An asset's value is recorded at the end of each year as $\$9000$, $\$7200$, $\$5760$ and $\$4608$. Which method of depreciation is being used, and why?

options.text: Declining balance, because each value is $0.8$ times the one before it.
Straight-line, because the value decreases every year.
options.why: Treats any falling value as straight-line; straight-line requires the same dollar loss each year.

options.text: Straight-line, because the value falls by $\$1800$ each year.
options.why: Uses the first year's drop as a fixed amount, but the later drops are $\$1440$ and $\$1152$.

options.text: Declining balance, because the value falls by $\$1800$ each year.
options.why: Names the right method with the straight-line reason; declining balance removes a fixed percentage.

questions.solution_text:
$7200 \div 9000 = 0.8$
$5760 \div 7200 = 0.8$
$4608 \div 5760 = 0.8$

Each value is the same **percentage** of the one before, so this is declining-balance depreciation at $20\%$ p.a.

questions.question_text: An asset costing $\$32\,000$ depreciates at $25\%$ p.a. by the declining-balance method. What annual straight-line amount would give the same value after $4$ years?

options.why: Took $25\%$ of the purchase price and used it as the fixed annual amount.
Divided the salvage value by $4$ instead of dividing the value lost.
Divided the value lost by $3$ years instead of $4$.

questions.question_text: A truck costing $\$95\,000$ is depreciated by $\$8000$ per year for $4$ years, after which the declining-balance method at $20\%$ p.a. is used. What is its value $8$ years after purchase?

options.why: Used straight-line depreciation for all $8$ years and ignored the change of method.
Stopped at the changeover and gave the value at the end of year $4$.
Applied only one year of declining balance instead of the remaining four.

questions.question_text: An asset bought for $\$46\,000$ has a straight-line salvage value of $\$19\,000$ after $6$ years. Under declining-balance depreciation at $15\%$ p.a., how much lower is its value after the same $6$ years, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Gave the declining-balance value itself instead of the difference between the two methods.
Gave the annual straight-line amount rather than the difference in the two salvage values.
Gave the total straight-line depreciation $46\,000 - 19\,000$.
